title: Bead Beating in Custom Buffer Followed by XP Bead Cleanup
author: Jason D Limberis
materials: rpm, °C, Centrifuge at max speed for 00:10:00

steps.title: Prepare Custom Triton Buffer
steps.instruction: Mix the following components to make the custom buffer: NaCl (5 M) 2 mL, Tris‑HCl pH 8.3 (1 M) 1 mL, EDTA pH 9.0 (0.5 M) 0.2 mL, Triton X‑100 1 mL, and H₂O 95.8 mL (total 100 mL). For a 100 mL preparation use Tris‑HCl 1 M pH 8 1 mL and EDTA 0.5 M 20 µL as indicated.

steps.title: Inactivate MGIT Tubes (if applicable)
steps.instruction: If the sample is in a MGIT tube, inactivate it by heating at 80 °C for 1 hour according to the South African National Health Laboratory Services (NHLS) standard operating procedures.

steps.title: Decontaminate Sample (if required)
steps.instruction: If the sample must be processed outside a BSL‑3 facility, decontaminate the original MGIT tube and media by heating at 80 °C for 1 hour following the NHLS SOP or your facility’s guidelines.

steps.title: Add DTT and Vortex Sample
steps.instruction: Add four volumes of 100 mM dithiothreitol (DTT) to the sputum sample, vortex for more than 30 seconds, then vortex the sample at maximum speed for 15 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Remove Supernatant and Resuspend Pellet
steps.instruction: Remove and discard the supernatant, then resuspend the remaining pellet in 350 µL of the custom Triton buffer prepared in Step 1.

steps.title: Prepare Bead Tubes and Beads
steps.instruction: Cut the bottom off a StarSted screw‑cap tube just below the inflection point. Cut the tip off a P1000 tip, make a wedge near the end, and wedge the prepared StarSted tube into it. Fill a sterile container (e.g., a Petri dish) with –0.1 mm Zirconia‑Silicate beads and use the prepared scoop to distribute the beads into 1.5 mL StarSted tubes (≈250 µL per tube).

steps.title: Transfer Sample to Bead Tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the inactivated bacterial suspension to a new, well‑labeled StarSted screw‑cap tube that already contains ~250 µL of Mini‑BeadBeater –0.1 mm Zirconia‑Silicate beads.

steps.title: Bead‑beat and Cleanup Cycle
steps.instruction: Perform the following sub‑steps as one complete cycle:

substeps.instruction: Bead‑beat the lysate at 6.5 m/s for 45 seconds, then place the tube on ice for a 2‑minute rest. (Repeat the bead‑beating/rest sequence as needed for the cycle.)
Add 250 µL (1.2× the lysate volume) of AMPure XP beads and mix by pipetting up and down ten times.
Centrifuge at maximum speed (10 000 rcf) at room temperature for 2 minutes. Transfer the clear supernatant to a new, well‑labeled tube, taking care not to transfer beads or debris.
Place the tube on a magnetic rack and wait ~2 minutes for the solution to clear.
Incubate the tube at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Discard the supernatant and wash the beads twice with freshly prepared 70 % (v/v) ethanol, avoiding disruption of the bead pellet.
Dry the beads briefly (~2 minutes); remove residual ethanol with a P10 pipette.
Resuspend the bead pellet in 20 µL of Low‑EDTA Tris buffer, ensuring all beads are in solution.
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Place the tube on the magnetic rack again, wait ~2 minutes for the solution to clear, and transfer the eluated DNA to a new, well‑labeled tube.

steps.title: Repeat Bead‑beat Cycles
steps.instruction: Repeat the entire "Bead‑beat and Cleanup Cycle" (Step 8) two additional times so that a total of three bead‑beating cycles are performed.
